claims.text: The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a uniform, fine lamellar eutectic microstructure.
The starting alloy's strength and plasticity are below industrial application requirements.
Post-solidification aging can activate secondary precipitation in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
A suitable aging temperature and duration will promote nucleation and moderate growth of nanoscale intermetallic precipitates.
The proposed aging treatment can form precipitates without coarsening the lamellar structure.
The precipitates formed by aging will be finely dispersed and coherent with the alloy matrix.
The precipitates will impede dislocation motion.
The precipitates will stabilize the microstructure during long-term mechanical loading and creep.
Impeded dislocation motion and microstructural stabilization will increase yield strength.
Impeded dislocation motion and microstructural stabilization will reduce room-temperature creep.
The aging-modified microstructure may have more favorable electrochemical properties.
More favorable electrochemical properties may enhance corrosion resistance under aggressive conditions.
Aged specimens are predicted to have higher yield strength than the as-solidified uniform lamellar alloy.
Aged specimens are predicted to have greater creep resistance than the as-solidified uniform lamellar alloy.
Aged specimens are predicted to maintain or improve corrosion behavior relative to the as-solidified alloy.
The proposed benefits are expected to apply under extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive conditions.
The treatment should not compromise the ductility required for fastener applications.
